en.name: Homemade salad dressing
en.summary: A homemade salad dressing has no preservatives and usually contains fresh ingredients — garlic, shallot, herbs, sometimes dairy or raw egg. It lives in the fridge and keeps about 2 weeks. Freezing is not the answer, because the emulsion breaks.
en.pantry: Homemade dressing does not belong on the counter. Raw garlic, shallot or herbs suspended in oil are low-acid produce in an oxygen-poor environment, which is exactly the situation that calls for refrigeration rather than a shelf, and any dressing containing dairy or raw egg is perishable outright. Follow the two-hour rule at the table — one hour if the room is above 32 °C (90 °F) — and put the jar back cold rather than leaving it out between meals.
en.fridge: Mix it, seal it and keep it at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, where it runs about 2 weeks. Use a clean jar rather than topping up an old batch, and label it with the date; two weeks passes quietly. Olive oil sets cloudy and thick in the cold — that is normal, and standing the jar out for a few minutes while you wash the leaves brings it back. Shake hard before each use. If your dressing contains raw egg, treat it as the perishable end and finish it sooner.
en.freezer: There is no freezer timeline for homemade dressing and freezing does not work: an oil-and-vinegar emulsion splits on thawing into oil with a layer of sediment, and a creamy one splits into oil and curds. Neither comes back with shaking. A dressing takes two minutes to make, so make it in the quantity you will use — and if you have too much, use it as a marinade for chicken or roasted vegetables rather than storing it colder.
spoilage: A rancid, crayon-like smell from the oil
Cloudiness, bubbles or fizzing, especially in a dressing containing garlic
Mould around the rim or on the surface
A sour or fermented smell rather than a sharp, clean one
tips: Make small batches; two weeks is the whole window.
Always use a clean jar — never top up an old batch with a new one.
Label the jar with the date you made it.
Let a cold jar stand a few minutes before shaking; olive oil thickens in the fridge.

faq.q: How long does homemade salad dressing last?
faq.a: About 2 weeks refrigerated at 4 °C or below in a sealed jar. Versions with raw egg should be finished sooner.

faq.q: Can you leave homemade dressing out of the fridge?
faq.a: No. Raw garlic or herbs in oil belong cold, and anything with dairy or raw egg is perishable. Keep it refrigerated.
There is no timeline and it does not work — the emulsion splits on thawing and will not shake back together.

faq.q: Why has my dressing gone solid in the fridge?
faq.a: Olive oil clouds and thickens when cold. Stand the jar out for a few minutes and shake; it is not spoilage.

zh.name: 自製沙拉醬
zh.summary: 自製沙拉醬沒有防腐劑，通常還含新鮮食材——蒜、紅蔥、香草，有時還有乳製品或生蛋。它屬於冰箱，大約可放 2 週。冷凍不是解方，因為乳化會破掉。
zh.pantry: 自製沙拉醬不該放在檯面上。生蒜、紅蔥或香草懸浮在油裡，是低酸性食材處在缺氧環境，正是必須冷藏而不是放架上的情況；而任何含乳製品或生蛋的醬本身就是易腐食品。餐桌上請遵守兩小時原則（室溫超過 32 °C 時為一小時），吃完就把罐子冰回去，不要留到下一餐。
zh.fridge: 調好、密封、放 4 °C 以下，大約 2 週。請用乾淨的罐子，不要把新的加進舊的裡續用，並標上日期；兩週會在你沒注意時悄悄過去。橄欖油在低溫下會變濁變稠——那是正常的，洗菜的時候把罐子放著回溫幾分鐘就好。每次使用前用力搖勻。如果醬裡有生蛋，請算在最容易壞的那一端，提早吃完。
zh.freezer: 自製沙拉醬沒有冷凍期限，而且冷凍行不通：油醋醬解凍後會分離成油和一層沉澱，奶香型的則會分離成油和凝結物，兩者都搖不回來。一份沙拉醬兩分鐘就能調好，所以調你用得完的量——真的調太多，就拿去當雞肉或烤蔬菜的醃料，而不是冰得更冷。
spoilage: 油發出油耗味或蠟筆味
出現混濁、氣泡或冒氣，含蒜的醬尤其要注意
聞起來發酸或有發酵味，而不是清爽的酸香
tips: 少量製作；整個窗口就只有兩週。
一定要用乾淨的罐子——不要把新醬加進舊醬裡。
冰過的罐子先放幾分鐘再搖；橄欖油在冰箱裡會變稠。

faq.q: 自製沙拉醬可以放多久？
faq.a: 密封放 4 °C 以下冷藏大約 2 週。含生蛋的版本要提早吃完。

faq.q: 自製沙拉醬可以放在室溫嗎？
faq.a: 不行。生蒜或香草泡在油裡必須低溫保存，含乳製品或生蛋的更是易腐。請全程冷藏。

faq.q: 自製沙拉醬可以冷凍嗎？
faq.a: 沒有對應期限，而且行不通——解凍後乳化會分離，搖也搖不回來。

faq.q: 沙拉醬在冰箱裡凝固了怎麼辦？
faq.a: 橄欖油遇冷會變濁變稠。放著回溫幾分鐘再搖勻即可，那不是腐壞。
